title: China's 9,200 km Border Road: Frozen East or Desert West? | China Travel Expert
description:
China's longest border road runs about 9,200 km. Frozen east or desert west — which end would you start?

The G331 traces China's northern frontier from Dandong on the eastern coast all the way to Altay in the far northwest — the country's second-longest national highway. Along the way it crosses the snow and forests of the northeast, the grasslands of Inner Mongolia, and the deserts and Altay peaks of Xinjiang. It's one leg of a planned ~26,000 km "Golden Outer Ring" border loop.

🧭 Expert Tip: Drive the northern grasslands in summer (roughly June–August) for peak green — the northeastern sections ice over in winter.
